purpose: Record why generic scalar Option support cannot be closed by a sentinel-only patch and define the bounded evidence needed before source authoring.

reviewedBuildIdentity.head: 55e9cbd954da8df52912b89840ead8d49c6011c7
reviewedBuildIdentity.note: The intervening commits changed documentation/provenance only; no compiler or product source changed.

evidenceRoutes: packages-ts/galerina-core-compiler/src/wat-emitter.ts: Option and Result values lower to opaque i32 handles; match, try-propagation and unwrap paths test the sentinel.
packages-ts/galerina-core-runtime-wasm/src/wasm-runtime.ts: __option_some returns the raw input and __option_none returns -1.
packages-ts/galerina-core-compiler/src/stdlib.ts: the interpreter keeps tagged some/none values and can carry arbitrary GalerinaValue payloads.
packages-ts/galerina-core-compiler/src/wat-emitter.ts: array get/first/last and String.charAt feed the same Option handle lane.

finding.currentEncoding: Some(x) is the raw i32 value; None is -1.
finding.collision: A legitimate negative Int payload collides with None.
affectedConsumers: Option match and try-propagation sign tests
for-in lowering that consumes array elements
finding.whySentinelOnlyFails: Changing the producer sentinel without coordinating every producer, consumer, host import, loop path and numeric width would either misclassify values or break existing iteration semantics.

minimum: Introduce receipt-bound option handles that preserve presence separately from payload.
Add typed host unwrap/access operations for every producer and consumer.
Preserve Int, Int64, Float64, String, record and nested payload widths.
Cover match, try-propagation, unwrapOr, get/first/last, charAt and for-in with differential interpreter/WASM vectors.
Prove invalid handles and malformed host inputs fail closed.

verdict: Generic scalar Option remains a shared ABI hold. Continue bounded product work that uses typed inert records; do not admit a new generic Option Fungi wave until the coordinated ABI repair has an exact scope and cross-producer/consumer evidence.
